title: FUSE unlink() EPERM investigation: why does delete-propagation succeed from cowork but fail from scheduled dome-mirror? Root-cause + inventory of fix paths, including moving delete-propagation to a different agent/mechanism if that's the right answer.

context.why_now: The Phase 2 transition finalized this morning (2026-07-08T05:52Z, commit 543350f6, DIRECTIVE-20260707-001 + PROP-124) put delete_propagation.enabled=true and drained the 1,137-file backlog manually. Steady state is now 8 candidates per dome-mirror cycle — great. But the first post-drain sentinel (2026-07-08T08:35Z, commit 408d77dd) revealed that scheduled dome-mirror CAN'T actually unlink FUSE files: EPERM, aborts to manifest-only, deleted=0. The operator-side manual drain worked (cowork session), but automated draining doesn't. So 'Phase 2 live' is currently an overstatement — it's more accurately 'Phase 2 opt-in from cowork, Phase 0 fallback from scheduled agents'. The gap is small in absolute terms (candidates accumulate ~30-40/day, months before another 500-abort would fire) but it's a real semantic mismatch: the code was designed to do the work automatically and doesn't.

evidence.aborted_verbatim: unlink-unsupported-on-fuse: EPERM: operation not permitted, unlink '/sessions/brave-eloquent-albattani/mnt/dome-model-review/monitor/integrity/sync-workspace-runs-2026-06-23T08-34-42Z.json' — falling back to manifest-only
evidence.documented_expectation_in_code: sync-workspace-step4c.js docstring L102-108: 'EPERM fallback: if FUSE refuses unlink (cross-session permission, no allow_cowork_file_delete grant), the pass records unlink-unsupported-on-fuse in the sentinel and stops. Manifest-only mode is still net positive — converts invisible accumulation into a visible deletion queue.' So the code EXPECTED this could happen and the design accepts it as a fallback. But that's a rationalization not a fix — Phase 2's purpose was actual automated deletion.
evidence.operator_side_success_evidence: Operator's cowork session (intelligent-brave-lamport) successfully rm'd 1,137 files at 05:49 UTC 2026-07-08 with 0 errors. Same FUSE mount, same physical paths, just different session context. The permission gap is scheduled-context vs cowork-context, not the FUSE mount itself.

questions_to_answer: Q1 — Why does unlink() succeed from cowork sessions but fail from scheduled agent sessions? Is it (a) an implicit allow_cowork_file_delete grant that only interactive cowork sessions get, (b) a FUSE mount option difference between session types, (c) a Unix uid/gid difference, (d) a mount-namespace difference, or (e) something else?
Q2 — Is allow_cowork_file_delete a per-session grant that can be programmatically requested at the start of a scheduled agent run? If yes, why doesn't dome-mirror.md already request it?

Q3 — Do OTHER agents ever need FUSE unlink? Poller writes to changes/, decider writes to decisions/, but do any of them ever need to DELETE from FUSE? If not, we may be the first case that needs this and there simply isn't an established pattern.

Q4 — What does the prune-integrity agent do that WORKS? It commits deletions via git (which doesn't need FUSE unlink) — is that the pattern to copy? Its Haiku prompt at monitor/prompts/... (script-only via SKILL.md — see monitor/scripts/prune-integrity.js) is the reference implementation of 'delete from git and let workspace-sync/dome-mirror propagate'.

Q5 — Is there a technical reason (safety, sandbox policy, session-lifecycle) why scheduled agents SHOULDN'T be able to unlink FUSE files? If yes, that's a strong signal to move delete-propagation elsewhere rather than try to enable it here.
part_A_root_cause.investigation_scope: Read the shipped code + docstrings + CLAUDE.md + any operator-directive or PROP that touched allow_cowork_file_delete. Do NOT attempt to modify sandbox policy or FUSE mount options — those are operator-infrastructure territory. Do a text-based investigation and report findings.
part_A_root_cause.output: Written analysis: monitor/tinker/reports/fuse-unlink-eperm-investigation-2026-07-08.md — plain-language answers to Q1-Q5 with evidence citations from the codebase.

candidates_to_evaluate.label: Request allow_cowork_file_delete grant at start of dome-mirror.md prompt
candidates_to_evaluate.if_feasible: Cheapest fix. dome-mirror.md gets a new 'Step 0: request delete grant' block; each scheduled run acquires the grant fresh.

candidates_to_evaluate.label: Move delete-propagation into workspace-sync (which may or may not have the same EPERM issue)
candidates_to_evaluate.if_feasible: workspace-sync already runs cross-session. If it can unlink, dome-mirror wraps thin over a workspace-sync deletion capability.

candidates_to_evaluate.label: Move delete-propagation OUT of scheduled agents entirely — a periodic operator-triggered cowork task (scheduled task with mcp__scheduled-tasks__create_scheduled_task that fires a cowork session monthly to run the drain)
candidates_to_evaluate.if_feasible: Guaranteed to work (proven today). Not automated in the pure sense, but eliminates the EPERM dependency. Cost: monthly operator attention (a few seconds).

candidates_to_evaluate.label: Redesign: git-side reconciliation only. prune-integrity already commits deletions to git; workspace-sync could implement 'FUSE files not in git = candidate for lazy deletion during next FUSE→git write cycle' via git-add-then-fs-check.
candidates_to_evaluate.if_feasible: Architecturally cleanest but most work. Might just push the EPERM problem to workspace-sync.

candidates_to_evaluate.label: Accept steady state. Document that periodic manual drain is the operational pattern. Add a canary check to integrity that fires at 200+ candidates so operator knows when to drain.
candidates_to_evaluate.if_feasible: Zero code work. Explicit acceptance of the constraint. Fine as long as steady state doesn't drift toward the abort threshold quickly.
